plainLanguage: Mtu hatakuwa criminally responsible ikiwa, wakati wa act au omission, disease affecting his mind ilisababisha moja ya effects tatu zilizotajwa: kutoweza kuelewa anachofanya; kutoweza kutambua kwamba hapaswi kufanya act/omission hiyo; au kutokuwa na control ya act/omission. Kuwa na mental disease peke yake hakutoshi kama haikusababisha mojawapo ya effects hizo kwa act/omission husika.
meaning: Section 13 inaunganisha disease affecting the mind na functional effect yake at the time of the act/omission. Subsection (1)(a)-(c) ni alternative statutory effects. Subsection (2) inasisitiza causal link: mtu anaweza kuwa na disease affecting the mind lakini bado akawa criminally responsible ikiwa disease hiyo haikusababisha effect yoyote iliyoorodheshwa kuhusu act/omission hiyo.
keyPoints: Timing ni muhimu: condition inaangaliwa at the time of doing the act or making the omission.
Lazima kuwe na disease affecting the mind.
Disease lazima iwe imesababisha angalau moja ya statutory effects katika (a), (b), au (c).
(a) inalenga capacity ya understanding; (b) appreciation kwamba act/omission ought not be done; (c) control.
Subsection (2) inaonyesha diagnosis/disease peke yake si automatic exemption from criminal responsibility.

legalTerms.meaning: Disease inayohusishwa na akili ambayo effect yake lazima ichunguzwe kwa tests za subsection (1).
Kutokuwa na uwezo wa kuelewa anachofanya wakati wa act/omission.
Kutokuwa na uwezo wa kutambua kwamba hapaswi kufanya act au omission hiyo.
Uwezo wa kudhibiti act au omission; section 13(1)(c) inatambua kutokuwa na control kama effect tofauti.

examples.title: Diagnosis bila statutory effect
examples.scenario: Accused ana diagnosed mental disease lakini evidence inaonyesha disease haikuathiri understanding, appreciation au control yake kuhusu act inayoshtakiwa.
examples.analysis: Section 13(2) inaonyesha kwamba existence ya disease pekee haitoshi; effect yake kwa act/omission ndiyo critical.

examples.title: Disease na inability to appreciate
examples.scenario: Evidence inaonyesha disease affecting the mind ilimfanya accused ashindwe appreciate kwamba hapaswi kufanya act hiyo wakati huo.
examples.analysis: Hii inaelekeza kwenye section 13(1)(b), lakini court lazima iamue facts na evidence ya case.

cases.name: Hilda Abel v Republic
cases.relevance: The Court held that insanity under section 13 is a question of fact inferable from circumstances and conduct, and that medical expert evidence is important but not automatically binding on the court.

cases.name: Republic v Maneno
cases.citation: Criminal Sessions Case No. 61 of 2001; [2005] TZHC 60
cases.relevance: The court considered psychiatric evidence that disease affecting the accused's mind deprived him of legally relevant capacity/control and applied the insanity framework.

cases.name: Frank Sadala v Republic
cases.relevance: A recent Court of Appeal decision treating section 13(1) insanity as an absolute defence when proved and emphasizing correct handling of insanity-related criminal procedure.

history.summary: The R.E. 2022 text records Act No. 31 of 1997 in the legislative history of section 13. The modern wording expressly separates understanding, appreciation of wrongfulness, and control.
notes: Older authorities remain useful only insofar as their propositions fit the current statutory wording.
Procedural questions about an accused's mental condition are also governed by the Criminal Procedure Act; they should not be confused with the substantive section 13 test.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo A
expertPerspectives.view: Psychiatric evidence can be central to proving disease and its effects, especially where it addresses the accused's condition at the material time.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo B
expertPerspectives.view: Insanity is ultimately a legal/factual determination under the statutory test. Hilda Abel demonstrates why a medical opinion does not mechanically decide the legal conclusion.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo C
expertPerspectives.view: The strongest analysis maps evidence separately onto understanding, appreciation and control rather than stopping at the existence of mental illness.

debateQuestion: Disease affecting the mind imethibitishwa vipi, na evidence inaunganisha disease hiyo na ipi kati ya effects za section 13(1)(a)-(c) katika material time?
disclaimer: Ufafanuzi huu si maandishi rasmi ya sheria.
